existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 keeps the `NutritionOrder` resource identity but substantially redesigns several local fields. The highest-impact issues are the mandatory `patient` to `subject` rename, schedule backbone restructuring, product fields switching to `CodeableReference`, removal of protocol instantiation fields, and loss/relocation of fluid/additive/enteral details. Confidence is high for structural deltas and lower for terminology semantics because expansions and official ConceptMaps were not available.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Main migration themes: (1) direct property renames (`patient`, `orderer`, enteral route/max volume/product fields); (2) structural rewrites for schedules and product/additive representation; (3) R6-to-R4 information loss from new optional workflow, performer, device, Group-subject, and NutritionProduct reference capabilities; and (4) terminology convergence from example bindings toward preferred SNOMED-oriented value sets.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local element presence, cardinality, type, binding-strength, and invariant changes because both R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions were present and compared directly. Confidence is medium for clinical terminology and narrative intent because official diffs, narrative implementation notes, full terminology expansions, and ConceptMaps were not available in the inspected local inputs. Inherited base-resource changes were deliberately excluded.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
NutritionOrder keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 11 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 0 potential hard break(s), 9 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 1 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 100/100, producing migration shape `major-model-remodel`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

12 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.
